all_rows.claim: `finite_domain_stable` Lean theorem advertised as finite-domain STABILITY (its premise was determinant non-negativity)
all_rows.kind: mis-operationalised (determinant nonnegativity advertised as stability; NOT vacuous premises)
all_rows.allowed: A theorem whose premise is determinant non-negativity was advertised as stability; the premise holds for unstable systems. It compiled and passed an axiom audit, which shows those checks do not establish that a statement means what its name says.
all_rows.witness: Codex commit b4e60db: planning/rethink/CODEX-21-CLAIM-FREEZE-REVIEW.md (original theorem paragraph) and the exact source snapshot artifacts/integration/codex-api/admissible-review/Admissible.lean (sha256 c51b98a8c4218c5e272223c5d710de0d765804d78beace544850f9749cf07236); messages/codex-price-probe-progress.md states the finding. Analytic witness J=diag(2,2), Du=Dv=1, L=pi: D(q)=(2-q)^2>=0 for all q satisfies the premise, yet mode n=1 (q=1) has both growth eigenvalues +1 (no new Lean compile of this witness is claimed). A stronger theorem `finite_domain_linearly_stable` was added later (commit 469874b; compiled by Codex at 7f9035a), so the historical defect was partly repaired. Earlier ledger text describing it as 'not_lt / saying nothing' came from THE-REFRAME and is NOT the accurate description.

limitations: No additive-genetic Fisher FTNS projection proved.
Regression corollary assumes orthogonal residual and positive focal variance and mean fitness; it does not establish causal benefit/cost.
Population interpretation requires normalized nonnegative weights; general algebra theorems allow broader inputs.
Author implemented and tested feasibility; not an independent statement-fidelity review.
Price/Hamilton relation is established mathematics; machine-checking priority not established.
